name: Social Baseline
description: Social proximity as metabolic resource regulator: being near an attachment figure reduces metabolic demand and stress. Proposed mechanism: social bonds act as allostatic buffers. Neural substrate speculative; evidence primarily behavioral and physiological.
key_references: Coan, J. A., & Sbarra, D. A. (2015). Social baseline theory: The social regulation of risk and uncertainty. Current Opinion in Psychology, 1, 87-91.
Eisenberger, N. I., & Cole, S. W. (2012). Social neuroscience and health: neurophysiological mechanisms linking social ties with physical health. Nature Neuroscience, 15(5), 669-674.
empirical_evidence: Behavioral: hand-holding reduces pain and stress responses. Social presence buffers autonomic responses to threat. fMRI shows reduced amygdala activation with partner present. Causal mechanism unclear: learned association, oxytocin release, or metabolic coupling? Limited evidence for dedicated neural circuit.

parameters.attachment_type: partner, parent, or general social group
